waQJEjiPWhg.title: How The Trumps Blew $1 Billion On Bitcoin
waQJEjiPWhg.transcript_text: Today on Forbes, how the Trumps blew $1 billion on Bitcoin. A leveraged bet at the top of a buy high cycle tends to do one thing, deepen the downside. In 2025, Donald Trump's family did just that, wagering billions of dollars on Bitcoin. It was May of 2025, and Trump had [music] just reentered the White House a few months prior. Crypto markets were going bananas. The president's sons, who had already made their father hundreds of millions richer with various Trump-themed digital assets, decided the next move was to make an institutional-sized bet on crypto's flagship currency, Bitcoin. At the time, a single Bitcoin cost $108,000. But with their father in the White House, the Trump sons predicted it would rise by more than 50% over the next year. On stage at a Bitcoin conference, Eric Trump declared confidently, "Quote, I think it clears $170,000." His brother, Donald Trump Jr., added, "Quote, I was going to say between 175 and 150." The siblings tasked with managing their father's business when he returned to the White House, believed in Bitcoin enough to put real money on the line. The president had placed his most valuable asset, >> [music] >> a 52% interest in the Trump Media and Technology Group, worth $2.6 billion, into a trust that left the elder Trump as the sole beneficiary, but technically handed control to Don Jr. Under the watch of the younger generation, the business strayed from its social media roots to make a massive [music] crypto bet. It sold $1.4 billion of stock and $1 billion of convertible bonds, then plowed the proceeds into Bitcoin. In the 2 [music] months between the deal's announcement and consummation, the price of Bitcoin kept climbing, hitting $119,000 by July, when Trump Media made its purchases. The transaction reshaped the president's portfolio, reducing his stake in Trump Media to 41%, [music] adding a mountain of debt, and turning Donald Trump into one of the world's biggest [music] Bitcoin investors. If the heirs' price targets held, the payoff was clear, roughly $1 billion of gains within a year. They didn't hold. Bitcoin stalled after the purchase. It remained somewhat steady for a few months, giving the Trump family little reason to celebrate, or worry, for that matter. In August, Trump Media poured another $114 million into a lesser-known cryptocurrency, Cronos. Then everything came tumbling down. In late November, a dip in the broader market pulled down riskier assets like Bitcoin and Cronos. By month's end, Trump Media's crypto assets, for which it had paid $2.4 billion, were worth an estimated $1.8 billion. Inside the company, efforts to stem the losses began. Trump Media hedged about 1/3 of its Bitcoin toward the end of the year, seemingly limiting potential downside and upside. January brought another unpleasant gut check. Fed Chairman Jerome Powell signaled, to the president's dismay, that interest rates would remain elevated. Bitcoin fell 5% in a day, dropping the value of Trump Media's holdings to an estimated $1.7 billion. The company extended its hedges, initially set to expire in March, to last until June. Just how much protection that has provided remains unclear. What is clear is that Trump Media wants to project confidence amid its troubles. Spokesperson Shannon Devine said in a statement, "Quote, our Bitcoin holdings reflect a long-term investment in this revolutionary digital currency, which we do not judge based on temporary cyclical downturns." But investors are already judging, harshly. Trump Media shares have fallen more sharply than Bitcoin itself, reflecting not just a loss of confidence in the crypto, but in the company. With Bitcoin at roughly $72,000 as of Wednesday, Trump Media's crypto stash sits in an estimated $1.4 billion, down $1 billion. The president's personal stake in Trump Media, meanwhile, has fallen $1.6 billion since his sons trumpeted their Bitcoin predictions on stage. For full coverage, check out Dan Alexander's piece on forbes.com. This is Kieran Meadows from Forbes. Thanks for tuning in.

e3FvKlH_2kg.title: Bitcoin Bulls Bet On Fed Chair Nominee Kevin Warsh As Central Bank Transition Nears
e3FvKlH_2kg.transcript_text: Bitcoin does not trade in isolation. It trades inside a macro environment shaped by the Federal Reserve. And President Trump has appointed Kevin Warsh as the next Fed chair, a former Fed governor who will now have major influence over interest rates, liquidity, and how the central bank responds to economic stress. Warsh has described Bitcoin as an important asset and even said, "If you're under 40, Bitcoin is your new gold." But it's also widely viewed as hawkish on rates and focused on monetary discipline. And tighter financial conditions are typically tough on risk assets like crypto. Kevin Warsh has been a QE hawk, where he's been very critical of the Fed printing money, which is actually consistent with Bitcoiners' view, and it's probably why he's pro-Bitcoin, cuz he sees the markets in a similar way to Bitcoin. The issue with him is that why and why it won't be an issue long-term is that the Fed is not the problem, the debt crisis. So, the US Treasury, Congress, they're the problem, and the Fed is kind of the doctor in this analogy, and they have to keep the markets functioning. And so, ultimately, Warsh will be will do what's needed to protect the dollar, and that's going to be printing more money. I think it's actually not correct that he's going to be as hawkish as people expect. And I'm really excited that there have been very positive mentions from Kevin Warsh about Bitcoin. And Kevin Warsh has been seen as more open to Bitcoin than past Fed leaders. Yet, prices fell after his nomination. How do you really see that? Well, I think that's a little bit of volatility in the market because they it's not just a signal about crypto, it's a signal about risk assets. There's a lot of folks that got used to that government printer being turned on. And unfortunately, while I think this new Fed chair has that mentality of I don't want to turn on the printers, QE is dangerous, we have boxed ourselves in over the last two decades, where the only option we have is to print our way out of difficult times, and it's almost become the go-to strategy. So, he's going to have to print his way through this next evolution. Stablecoins will come into it, cryptocurrency will be a part of it. I wouldn't be surprised if more risk assets are having a difficult time with this transition. Once there's a little bit more clarity, which is not just him walking in office and putting his stance out as the new Fed chair, but also the Clarity Act itself, that's almost through the Senate, but it's getting a little bit of pork and fat tossed on top of it. When those two things come through, I think, like others, Kevin O'Leary said, "There's about a trillion dollars waiting to walk into this space once they have that clarity." Kevin Warsh faces the same dilemma that every Fed chair faces, which is that we've got so much debt, we've got such high burdens with this interest expense, and I think no matter what, he's going to have to bring interest rates down, and he's going to be probably more dovish than people expect. Investors are now weighing whether a more crypto-friendly tone at the Fed can meaningfully support Bitcoin, or whether interest rates and liquidity will continue to dictate the direction of the trade. For Investors Business Daily, I'm Claire O'Connor.
